selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is said about the basic materials of creation and where they are found?
questions.answer: They are spread across the whole earth.

questions.question: What is said about each kind of created thing that shows a sign of oneness?
questions.answer: Each kind is found widely over the earth in a united way.

questions.question: What does the spread of the elements and species show clearly?
questions.answer: It shows they all belong to one Creator.

questions.question: How are the elements described in relation to that one Creator?
questions.answer: They are like strong servants under His command.

questions.question: How are the species and their many individual members described?
questions.answer: They are like orderly soldiers serving under one ruler.

questions.question: What does this comparison to servants and soldiers help us understand?
questions.answer: It helps us understand that one powerful Lord controls them all.

questions.question: Why does the passage connect wide spread across the earth with unity instead of many owners?
questions.answer: Because things that work together in the same way across the earth point to one owner, not many separate ones.

questions.question: What quality of the Creator is especially highlighted by commanding huge elements and many species?
questions.answer: His unique power and unmatched authority.

questions.question: Does the passage give a long full proof here or only a short reminder?
questions.answer: It gives only a short reminder.

questions.question: After mentioning this truth, what does the passage say the traveler does?
questions.answer: He prepares to speak from the strong faith and joy he gained from the five truths.

questions.question: What fills the whole earth according to the passage?
questions.answer: The elements that make up created things fill the earth.

questions.question: What is special about the different kinds of living or created things mentioned here?
questions.answer: They carry signs that point to oneness and are spread all over the earth.

questions.question: When the passage says these species almost take over the earth, what idea is it giving?
questions.answer: It means they are found everywhere in a broad and powerful way.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the earthwide spread of elements and species?
questions.answer: They must come from one being and belong to Him.

questions.question: What two relationships do these things have to that one being?
questions.answer: They are His products and also His servants.

questions.question: What does calling the elements obedient teach us about them?
questions.answer: They do not act on their own but follow Allah’s command.

questions.question: What does calling the species disciplined soldiers teach us about creation?
questions.answer: It shows there is order, control, and one commander over them.

questions.question: Which is a better summary of the main point: many powers are competing, or one power is ruling?
questions.answer: One power is ruling.

questions.question: What reason is given for not explaining this truth in detail here?
questions.answer: It has already been explained in other parts of the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What writing choice appears at the end of this paragraph?
questions.answer: The explanation is kept brief because the matter was already explained elsewhere.

questions.question: According to the passage, what covers the earth from among the materials of creation?
questions.answer: The basic elements of creation cover the earth.

questions.question: What is true of each species that points to unity?
questions.answer: Each one is spread throughout the earth as a single kind.

questions.question: How does the passage move from observation to belief?
questions.answer: It looks at the worldwide spread of things and concludes that one Creator made and owns them.

questions.question: What does the word “property” mean in this passage?
questions.answer: It means these things belong to one Lord.
